phases.name: Security Engine & Zero Trust
phases.goal: Zero-trust layering verified by tests (WAF -> AuthN -> AuthZ -> Tenant -> Sandbox -> Egress -> DB policy -> Encrypted data).
deliverables: Edge: Redis-backed rate limiting (shared across instances, was in-memory) + a stricter dedicated limit on /v1/auth/*; known-scanner-user-agent WAF denylist; body-size + schema validation unchanged from Phase 1

AuthN: real, working local email+password+TOTP-MFA staff auth (argon2id, <=15-min HS256 access tokens, rotating opaque refresh tokens with reuse detection incl. the concurrent-refresh race); IdentityProvider OIDC seam + NotConfiguredIdentityProvider (no external provider chosen yet, matching the AIProvider/WhatsAppClient precedent) — see docs/SECURITY-MODEL.md §3
AuthZ: RBAC role->permission matrix + ABAC tenant-match policy engine (authorize()), enforced as Fastify preHandlers (authenticate, requirePermission) on every new admin route

Tenant isolation: Postgres RLS (ENABLE+FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY) on every tenant-scoped table old and new, keyed on a per-transaction app.tenant_id session setting (withTenantContext()); real least-privilege ai_concierge_api/ai_concierge_worker DB roles (no DELETE/DDL/BYPASSRLS); cross-tenant negative tests proven against the real scoped role connection, not just app-level filtering

AI sandbox: tool permission matrix seam (packages/ai/src/sandbox) -- no AIProvider does real LLM tool-calling yet, so nothing exists to gate for real; egress allowlist unchanged from Phase 1 (ssrfSafeFetch); injection defences unchanged from Phase 1-2; output DLP is a tripwire on outbound text (should never fire today -- every reply is template-built, no free-text AI generation exists) -- see docs/SECURITY-MODEL.md §3 for the honest scope split

Data: TLS at the edge (platform-terminated); AES-256-GCM field-level encryption applied to the one real secret this phase introduces (the MFA TOTP seed) -- passport/licence-number encryption reuses the same primitive once a document pipeline exists; docs/SECURITY-MODEL.md's key rotation runbook

Detection & response: SecurityEvent append-only stream + five anomaly/detection rules (login lockout, tenant-wide login velocity, token-reuse, mass-export, permission-denied/cross-tenant) with automatic response (immediate session revocation via a Redis family-revocation set, closing the residual-JWT-validity window) and manual response (POST /v1/users/:id/lock|unlock); GET /v1/security-events is the current T4 escalation surface until a full EscalationCase model exists
